### Prerequisites

This game shows how the multiplication tables of 3 and 9 are related: 9 × n = 3 × 3 × n, so the table of 9 is the table of 3 multiplied by 3 — every result of the table of 9 is a result of the table of 3 with the multiplier tripled. Before you play, we suggest reviewing:

- **Learning the Multiplication Table (8 and 9)**: a simple introduction to multiplying by eight and by nine with an octagon and an enneagon (<htcite0>)

With the table of 9 fresh in your memory, you are ready to see how each of its results is also a result of the table of 3.

### Introduction

The table of 9 is built from the table of 3. Nine is 3 × 3, so we reach a multiple of 9 by multiplying by 3 twice: for 9 × 4, take 3 × 4 = 12, then 12 × 3 = 36. In this game, the left column shows that road — 3 × 3 × n = 9 × n — and the right column shows the product it reaches, drawn as groups of nine characters. Once you can walk this road, the table of 9 stops being a new table: it is only the table of 3 one more multiplication by 3 away.

### General rules

The table of 9 is the table of 3 multiplied by 3. Multiplying by 9 is the same as multiplying by 3 twice in a row — 9 × n = 3 × 3 × n. That is why every result of the table of 9 is also a result of the table of 3: for n = 4, 3 × 3 × 4 = 36 and 9 × 4 = 36; three groups of three groups of four are nine groups of four.

This game makes that relationship visible. On the left, you will see an equality like 3 × 3 × 4 = 9 × 4; on the right, its result appears together with a picture of groups of characters, drawn as rectangles with nine characters each — the picture of the 9 × n side of the equality.

The game has three levels:

- **Level 1**: three equalities written as 3 × 3 × n = 9 × n, from the first third of the table of 9 (results 9 to 27).
- **Level 2**: three equalities written as 3 × 3 × n = 9 × n, from the second third of the table of 9 (results 36 to 54).
- **Level 3**: three equalities written as 3 × 3 × n = 9 × n, from the last third of the table of 9 (results 63 to 81).

Above the game, a selector chooses the image used in the groups: **🎲 Random** draws a random object from the multiplication tables in every new exercise, or you can select one specific image — the same ones used in the multiplication tables — and every group uses it while you play.

To play, select an equality on the left and then its result on the right. If the pair is correct, both stay highlighted. When you match every pair, you complete the level and can move on to the next one.

### The Game

Match each equality on the left with its result on the right. The result also appears as groups of characters, so you can count them to check your answer — every rectangle holds nine characters, exactly like the 9 × n side of the equality. If a pair is wrong, a message will ask you to try again.
